text:
Maria: quick helm question — trying to wire an optional secret into envFrom from values.yaml. We want to support two modes: (1) user sets values.service.secret.name and helm renders an envFrom secretRef, or (2) user leaves that blank and an ExternalSecret will create the secret later. Right now the chart renders an empty secretRef name and the pod fails. Paste of values & template i'm using:

values.yaml snippet:

service:
  image: repo/app:1.2
  envFromSecretName: ""   # optional, either set this or let external-secret create it

templates/deployment.yaml snippet:

```yaml
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.service.envFromSecretName }}
      optional: true
```

This renders `name: ` (empty) when not set and k8s rejects it. Any good patterns to avoid rendering the whole envFrom block when the value is empty, but still allow optional: true when provided?

Sam: easiest is to guard the block with an if. Helm treats empty string as falsey, so:

```helm
{{- if .Values.service.envFromSecretName }}
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ .Values.service.envFromSecretName | quote }}
    optional: true
{{- end }}
```

That prevents an empty name from being rendered. Also put a small note in values.schema (or README) that empty string = absent. :thumbsup:

Noah: another pattern if you want to accept either `envFromSecretName` or `externalSecret.enabled` flag is to use a helper func to choose the source. e.g. in _helpers.tpl:

```helm
{{- define "service.envFromIf" -}}
{{- $name := .Values.service.envFromSecretName -}}
{{- if and (not $name) .Values.service.externalSecret.enabled }}
  # skip: external-secret will create it, do nothing
{{- else if $name }}
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ $name | quote }}
    optional: true
{{- end }}
{{- end -}}
```

Then call `{{ include "service.envFromIf" . }}`. Keeps template tidy.

Alice: small gotcha — `lookup` can query the cluster for a Secret at render/install time, but that only works during `helm install/upgrade` (not `helm template`) and can break chart verification in CI. I recommend not relying on `lookup` for chart templating unless you need immediate existence checks.

Also if you want to avoid repeating `optional: true` across a few places, you can render a compact block that sets optional only when name is present:

```helm
{{- if .Values.service.envFromSecretName }}
  envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.service.envFromSecretName | quote }}
      optional: true
{{- end }}
```

Maria: ah cool. I wasn't aware empty string is falsey in helm templates — that solves it. One follow-up: our values.yaml default is "". Are there cases where users accidentally set null and it still renders? Should we normalize with `default`?

Sam: good call. Use the `default`/`required` or coalesce pattern: `{{- $name := default "" .Values.service.envFromSecretName }}` then `if $name` works. Or shorter: `if (default "" .Values.service.envFromSecretName)`. But I prefer assigning to a local var so you can reuse.

Noah: also consider adding a simple unit test with helm unittest or a `helm template` CI job that renders with an empty value to ensure no empty name appears. Quick GH action: `helm template ./charts/service --set service.envFromSecretName= > /dev/null` and check output for `name: \n` pattern.

devops-bot: CI: lint passed for chart/service on branch feature/optional-envfrom (build 842) :white_check_mark:

Maria: thanks all — i'll update the helper and add a templating unit test. Marking this resolved. :raised_hands:
